Original practice questions written for testing the app. Not taken from any official UPTET paper.

text.en: According to Jean Piaget, in which stage does a child begin to think logically about concrete objects and events (about 7 to 11 years)?
text.hi: जीन पियाजे के अनुसार, किस अवस्था में बच्चा मूर्त वस्तुओं और घटनाओं के बारे में तार्किक रूप से सोचना शुरू करता है (लगभग 7 से 11 वर्ष)?

explanation.en: Piaget described four stages: sensorimotor (0–2 years), pre-operational (2–7), concrete operational (7–11) and formal operational (11 onwards). Logical thinking about concrete objects, including conservation, develops in the concrete operational stage; abstract reasoning comes later, in the formal operational stage.
explanation.hi: पियाजे ने चार अवस्थाएँ बताईं: संवेदी-गामक (0–2 वर्ष), पूर्व-संक्रियात्मक (2–7 वर्ष), मूर्त संक्रियात्मक (7–11 वर्ष) और औपचारिक संक्रियात्मक (11 वर्ष से आगे)। मूर्त वस्तुओं के बारे में तार्किक चिंतन, जैसे संरक्षण (conservation) की समझ, मूर्त संक्रियात्मक अवस्था में विकसित होता है; अमूर्त चिंतन बाद में औपचारिक संक्रियात्मक अवस्था में आता है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Who gave the concept of the 'Zone of Proximal Development' (ZPD)?
text.hi: 'समीपस्थ विकास का क्षेत्र' (ZPD) की अवधारणा किसने दी?

explanation.en: Lev Vygotsky described the ZPD as the gap between what a learner can do alone and what they can do with help from a more knowledgeable person. Support given within this zone is often called scaffolding.
explanation.hi: लेव वाइगोत्स्की के अनुसार ZPD वह अंतर है जो बच्चा स्वयं कर सकता है और जो वह किसी अधिक जानकार व्यक्ति की सहायता से कर सकता है। इस क्षेत्र में दी गई सहायता को प्रायः 'पाड़' (scaffolding) कहा जाता है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: The theory of operant conditioning is associated with:
text.hi: क्रियाप्रसूत अनुबंधन (ऑपरेंट कंडीशनिंग) का सिद्धांत किससे संबंधित है?

explanation.en: B. F. Skinner developed operant conditioning: behaviour that is followed by reinforcement becomes more likely to be repeated. Pavlov is linked with classical conditioning, Köhler with insight learning and Bandura with observational (social) learning.
explanation.hi: बी. एफ. स्किनर ने क्रियाप्रसूत अनुबंधन का सिद्धांत दिया: जिस व्यवहार के बाद पुनर्बलन मिलता है, उसके दोहराए जाने की संभावना बढ़ जाती है। पावलोव शास्त्रीय अनुबंधन से, कोहलर सूझ द्वारा अधिगम से और बंडूरा अवलोकन (सामाजिक) अधिगम से जुड़े हैं।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Lawrence Kohlberg's stage theory is mainly about:
text.hi: लॉरेंस कोहलबर्ग का अवस्था सिद्धांत मुख्य रूप से किससे संबंधित है?

explanation.en: Kohlberg described moral development in three levels — pre-conventional, conventional and post-conventional — each with two stages, based on how people reason about right and wrong.
explanation.hi: कोहलबर्ग ने नैतिक विकास के तीन स्तर बताए — पूर्व-परंपरागत, परंपरागत और उत्तर-परंपरागत — और प्रत्येक स्तर में दो अवस्थाएँ हैं। यह इस पर आधारित है कि व्यक्ति सही और गलत के बारे में कैसे तर्क करता है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Learning by observing and imitating others is a central idea of the theory given by:
text.hi: दूसरों को देखकर और उनका अनुकरण करके सीखना किसके द्वारा दिए गए सिद्धांत का मुख्य विचार है?

explanation.en: Albert Bandura's social learning theory explains that children learn by watching models and imitating them, as shown in his Bobo doll experiment. Bruner is known for discovery learning and Erikson for psychosocial development.
explanation.hi: अल्बर्ट बंडूरा के सामाजिक अधिगम सिद्धांत के अनुसार बच्चे दूसरों (मॉडल) को देखकर और उनका अनुकरण करके सीखते हैं, जैसा उनके बोबो डॉल प्रयोग में दिखा। ब्रूनर खोज द्वारा अधिगम के लिए और एरिक्सन मनोसामाजिक विकास के लिए जाने जाते हैं।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Howard Gardner is best known for the theory of:
text.hi: हावर्ड गार्डनर किस सिद्धांत के लिए सबसे अधिक जाने जाते हैं?

explanation.en: Gardner proposed that intelligence is not a single ability but several, such as linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, musical, bodily-kinaesthetic, interpersonal, intrapersonal and naturalistic. The hierarchy of needs is Maslow's theory.
explanation.hi: गार्डनर के अनुसार बुद्धि एक ही योग्यता नहीं, बल्कि कई प्रकार की होती है, जैसे भाषाई, तार्किक-गणितीय, स्थानिक, संगीतात्मक, शारीरिक-गतिसंवेदी, अंतर्वैयक्तिक, अंतःवैयक्तिक और प्रकृतिवादी। आवश्यकताओं का पदानुक्रम मास्लो का सिद्धांत है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: A child of normal intelligence has persistent difficulty in reading — recognising words, decoding and spelling. This is most likely:
text.hi: सामान्य बुद्धि वाले एक बच्चे को पढ़ने में लगातार कठिनाई होती है — शब्द पहचानने, अक्षरों को जोड़कर पढ़ने और वर्तनी में। इसकी सबसे अधिक संभावना है:

explanation.en: Dyslexia is a specific learning disability related to reading. Dyscalculia relates to mathematics, dysgraphia to writing, and dyspraxia to the coordination of movements.
explanation.hi: डिस्लेक्सिया पढ़ने से संबंधित एक विशिष्ट अधिगम अक्षमता है। डिस्कैलकुलिया गणित से, डिस्ग्राफिया लेखन से और डिस्प्रैक्सिया गतियों के समन्वय से संबंधित है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, free and compulsory education is the right of children aged:
text.hi: निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009 के अंतर्गत किस आयु वर्ग के बच्चों को निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का अधिकार है?

explanation.en: The RTE Act, 2009 gives every child aged 6 to 14 years the right to free and compulsory elementary education, giving effect to Article 21A of the Constitution. It came into force on 1 April 2010.
explanation.hi: शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009 के अनुसार 6 से 14 वर्ष के प्रत्येक बच्चे को निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य प्रारंभिक शिक्षा का अधिकार है। यह संविधान के अनुच्छेद 21क को लागू करता है और 1 अप्रैल 2010 से प्रभावी हुआ।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Which statement best describes inclusive education?
text.hi: समावेशी शिक्षा का सबसे उपयुक्त वर्णन कौन-सा कथन करता है?

text.en: Children with disabilities study only in separate special schools.
text.hi: दिव्यांग बच्चे केवल अलग विशेष विद्यालयों में पढ़ते हैं।

text.en: All children, including those with special needs, learn together in regular classrooms with suitable support.
text.hi: विशेष आवश्यकता वाले बच्चों सहित सभी बच्चे उपयुक्त सहायता के साथ सामान्य कक्षाओं में साथ-साथ सीखते हैं।
केवल उच्च उपलब्धि वाले विद्यार्थियों को प्रवेश दिया जाता है।

text.en: Every child follows exactly the same pace and method.
text.hi: हर बच्चा बिल्कुल एक ही गति और एक ही विधि से सीखता है।

explanation.en: Inclusive education means educating all children together in regular schools, adapting teaching, materials and support so that every child — including children with disabilities — can participate and learn.
explanation.hi: समावेशी शिक्षा का अर्थ है सभी बच्चों को सामान्य विद्यालयों में साथ-साथ पढ़ाना और शिक्षण, सामग्री व सहायता को इस प्रकार ढालना कि दिव्यांग बच्चों सहित हर बच्चा भाग ले सके और सीख सके।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: What is the LCM of 12 and 18?
text.hi: 12 और 18 का लघुत्तम समापवर्त्य (LCM) क्या है?

explanation.en: 12 = 2² × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3². The LCM takes the highest power of each prime: 2² × 3² = 36. (6 is their HCF, and 216 is just their product.)
explanation.hi: 12 = 2² × 3 और 18 = 2 × 3²। LCM में प्रत्येक अभाज्य गुणनखंड की सबसे बड़ी घात ली जाती है: 2² × 3² = 36। (6 इनका महत्तम समापवर्तक (HCF) है और 216 केवल इनका गुणनफल है।)

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Which is the smallest prime number?
text.hi: सबसे छोटी अभाज्य संख्या कौन-सी है?

explanation.en: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime. 2 is the smallest prime and the only even prime.
explanation.hi: अभाज्य संख्या के ठीक दो गुणनखंड होते हैं: 1 और स्वयं वह संख्या। 1 का केवल एक गुणनखंड है, इसलिए वह अभाज्य नहीं है। 2 सबसे छोटी और एकमात्र सम अभाज्य संख्या है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: What is the place value of 7 in 4,73,215?

explanation.en: In 4,73,215 the digit 7 is in the ten-thousands place, so its place value is 7 × 10,000 = 70,000. Its face value is 7.
explanation.hi: 4,73,215 में 7 दस हज़ार के स्थान पर है, इसलिए उसका स्थानीय मान 7 × 10,000 = 70,000 है। उसका जातीय (अंकित) मान 7 है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

explanation.en: Write both fractions with the denominator 8: 3/4 = 6/8. Then 6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8.

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.
Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: The perimeter of a square is 48 cm. What is its area?
text.hi: एक वर्ग का परिमाप 48 सेमी है। उसका क्षेत्रफल क्या है?

explanation.en: Side = perimeter ÷ 4 = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm. Area = side × side = 12 × 12 = 144 cm².

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: What is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle?
text.hi: किसी त्रिभुज के तीनों अंतःकोणों का योग कितना होता है?

explanation.en: The three interior angles of any triangle always add up to 180°. The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°.
explanation.hi: किसी भी त्रिभुज के तीनों अंतःकोणों का योग सदैव 180° होता है। चतुर्भुज के कोणों का योग 360° होता है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
text.hi: एक वर्ग में सममिति की कितनी रेखाएँ होती हैं?

explanation.en: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: 2 diagonals and 2 lines joining the midpoints of opposite sides.
explanation.hi: वर्ग में सममिति की 4 रेखाएँ होती हैं: 2 विकर्ण और सम्मुख भुजाओं के मध्य-बिंदुओं को मिलाने वाली 2 रेखाएँ।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Green plants make their own food by the process of:
text.hi: हरे पौधे किस प्रक्रिया द्वारा अपना भोजन स्वयं बनाते हैं?

explanation.en: In photosynthesis, green plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide and water, with the help of chlorophyll, to make food (glucose) and release oxygen. Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaves.
explanation.hi: प्रकाश संश्लेषण में हरे पौधे क्लोरोफिल की सहायता से सूर्य के प्रकाश, कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड और जल का उपयोग करके भोजन (ग्लूकोज़) बनाते हैं और ऑक्सीजन छोड़ते हैं। वाष्पोत्सर्जन पत्तियों से जलवाष्प निकलने की प्रक्रिया है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Which vitamin is made in our skin when it is exposed to sunlight?
text.hi: सूर्य के प्रकाश के संपर्क में आने पर हमारी त्वचा में कौन-सा विटामिन बनता है?

explanation.en: When sunlight (ultraviolet-B rays) falls on the skin, the body makes vitamin D, which helps it absorb calcium for strong bones and teeth.
explanation.hi: जब सूर्य का प्रकाश (पराबैंगनी-B किरणें) त्वचा पर पड़ता है, तो शरीर विटामिन D बनाता है, जो मज़बूत हड्डियों और दाँतों के लिए कैल्शियम के अवशोषण में सहायता करता है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Which organ pumps blood to all parts of the body?
text.hi: शरीर के सभी भागों तक रक्त को कौन-सा अंग पंप करता है?

explanation.en: The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood through blood vessels to every part of the body. The lungs exchange gases, the kidneys filter blood to make urine, and the liver has many roles, including making bile.
explanation.hi: हृदय एक मांसपेशीय अंग है जो रक्त वाहिकाओं के माध्यम से शरीर के हर भाग तक रक्त पंप करता है। फेफड़े गैसों का आदान-प्रदान करते हैं, गुर्दे रक्त को छानकर मूत्र बनाते हैं और यकृत पित्त बनाने सहित कई कार्य करता है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Which of these animals is a mammal?
text.hi: इनमें से कौन-सा जंतु स्तनधारी है?

explanation.en: Bats are mammals: they have hair and feed their young on milk. Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly. A shark is a fish, a penguin is a bird and a crocodile is a reptile.
explanation.hi: चमगादड़ स्तनधारी है: उसके शरीर पर बाल होते हैं और वह अपने बच्चों को दूध पिलाता है। चमगादड़ ही ऐसा स्तनधारी है जो वास्तव में उड़ सकता है। शार्क एक मछली, पेंगुइन एक पक्षी और मगरमच्छ एक सरीसृप है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: The ozone layer, which protects us from harmful ultraviolet rays, is found mainly in the:
text.hi: हानिकारक पराबैंगनी किरणों से हमारी रक्षा करने वाली ओज़ोन परत मुख्य रूप से कहाँ पाई जाती है?

explanation.en: Most of the atmosphere's ozone is in the stratosphere, roughly 15 to 35 km above the Earth. It absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.
explanation.hi: वायुमंडल की अधिकांश ओज़ोन समतापमंडल में, पृथ्वी से लगभग 15 से 35 किमी की ऊँचाई पर होती है। यह सूर्य की हानिकारक पराबैंगनी किरणों के बड़े भाग को अवशोषित कर लेती है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Which gas makes up the largest part of the Earth's atmosphere?
text.hi: पृथ्वी के वायुमंडल का सबसे बड़ा भाग किस गैस का है?

explanation.en: Dry air is about 78% nitrogen and about 21% oxygen. Argon is just under 1%, and carbon dioxide is only about 0.04%.
explanation.hi: शुष्क वायु में लगभग 78% नाइट्रोजन और लगभग 21% ऑक्सीजन होती है। आर्गन 1% से थोड़ा कम है और कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड केवल लगभग 0.04% है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Which of these is a renewable source of energy?
text.hi: इनमें से कौन-सा ऊर्जा का नवीकरणीय स्रोत है?

explanation.en: Solar energy comes from the Sun and is continuously replenished. Coal, petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels that took millions of years to form, so they cannot be replaced once used up.
explanation.hi: सौर ऊर्जा सूर्य से मिलती है और लगातार उपलब्ध रहती है। कोयला, पेट्रोलियम और प्राकृतिक गैस जीवाश्म ईंधन हैं, जिन्हें बनने में लाखों वर्ष लगे, इसलिए एक बार समाप्त होने पर उनकी भरपाई नहीं हो सकती।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Choose the correct article: "She is ___ honest teacher."
text.hi: सही आर्टिकल चुनिए: "She is ___ honest teacher."

explanation.en: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound because the 'h' is silent, so we use 'an'.
explanation.hi: 'Honest' में 'h' मूक (silent) है, इसलिए इसका उच्चारण स्वर ध्वनि से शुरू होता है (ऑनेस्ट)। स्वर ध्वनि से पहले 'an' का प्रयोग होता है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: In the sentence "She sings beautifully", the word 'beautifully' is:
text.hi: वाक्य "She sings beautifully" में 'beautifully' शब्द है:

explanation.en: 'Beautifully' tells us how she sings, so it describes the verb 'sings'. Words that describe verbs are adverbs.
explanation.hi: 'Beautifully' बताता है कि वह कैसे गाती है, अर्थात यह क्रिया 'sings' की विशेषता बताता है। क्रिया की विशेषता बताने वाले शब्द क्रियाविशेषण (Adverb) होते हैं।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

explanation.en: 'Child' has an irregular plural: 'children'. 'Childrens' is incorrect; the possessive form is written 'children's'.
explanation.hi: 'Child' का बहुवचन अनियमित है: 'children'। 'Childrens' गलत है; स्वामित्व (possessive) रूप 'children's' लिखा जाता है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Fill in the blank: "Yesterday, he ___ to the market."
text.hi: रिक्त स्थान भरिए: "Yesterday, he ___ to the market."

explanation.en: 'Yesterday' shows the action happened in the past, so we use the simple past tense of 'go', which is 'went'. 'Gone' is the past participle and needs a helping verb (has/had gone).
explanation.hi: 'Yesterday' बताता है कि कार्य भूतकाल में हुआ, इसलिए 'go' का simple past रूप 'went' प्रयोग होगा। 'Gone' past participle है, जिसके साथ सहायक क्रिया चाहिए (has/had gone)।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Which of these is a synonym of 'सूर्य' (sun)?

explanation.en: दिनकर ('maker of the day') means the sun. निशाकर, सुधाकर and हिमकर are all synonyms of the moon (चंद्रमा).
explanation.hi: दिनकर (दिन करने वाला) का अर्थ सूर्य है। निशाकर, सुधाकर और हिमकर — ये सभी चंद्रमा के पर्यायवाची हैं।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

explanation.en: उत्थान means rise and पतन means fall, so they are opposites. उन्नति and प्रगति have a similar meaning to उत्थान, and the opposite of आरोहण (climbing up) is अवरोहण.
explanation.hi: उत्थान का अर्थ है ऊपर उठना और पतन का अर्थ है गिरना, इसलिए ये विलोम हैं। उन्नति और प्रगति उत्थान के समान अर्थ वाले शब्द हैं, तथा आरोहण का विलोम अवरोहण है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: What is the correct sandhi-viched (split) of 'विद्यालय'?

explanation.en: विद्या + आलय = विद्यालय. Here आ + आ combine into आ, which is दीर्घ स्वर संधि (long-vowel sandhi).
explanation.hi: विद्या + आलय = विद्यालय। यहाँ आ + आ मिलकर आ बन जाते हैं, इसलिए यह दीर्घ स्वर संधि है।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en: Which word is NOT a synonym of 'कमल' (lotus)?
text.hi: इनमें से कौन-सा शब्द 'कमल' का पर्यायवाची नहीं है?

explanation.en: पंकज, जलज and नीरज all mean lotus (a flower born in mud or water). जलद means 'giver of water', i.e. a cloud (बादल).
explanation.hi: पंकज, जलज और नीरज — तीनों कमल के पर्यायवाची हैं (कीचड़ या जल में उत्पन्न होने वाला)। जलद का अर्थ है 'जल देने वाला', अर्थात बादल।

questions.source: Original sample question written for app testing; not from an official UPTET paper.

text.en:
Read the following statements :
Assertion (A) : Some children have characteristics that resemble their parents while others are markedly different from their parents.
Reason (R) : Working out how much of any characteristic is due to nature or genes and how much is due to nurture or environment is a complex issue.
Choose the correct option.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are false.

explanation.en: Children inherit genes from both parents and also grow up in their own environments. Because each trait comes from a complex mix of heredity (nature) and environment (nurture), some children closely resemble their parents while others differ markedly. So R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 1. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following statements about development is correct?
Development in children can be predicted very accurately.
Development is a simple and unitary process.
Development can always be measured precisely.

explanation.en: Development takes place in many domains at once — physical, cognitive, social and emotional (multidimensional) — and some abilities grow while others decline (multidirectional). It is not a simple single process, it cannot be predicted very accurately, and it cannot always be measured precisely.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 2. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Read the following statements :
Assertion (A) : The ability to comprehend and speak depends on the physical development of the mouth and brain.
Reason (R) : Emotional development is related to physical growth.
Choose the correct option.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are false.

explanation.en: Development in one domain is linked to the others. Understanding and producing speech depends on the maturing of the brain and speech organs, and emotional development is likewise tied to physical growth. The official key treats R as explaining A because both describe how physical growth underlies other areas of development.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 3. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Most children can speak five-six coherent sentences at

explanation.en: Speech develops quickly in the early years: around one year children say single words, and by about three years most can speak in short, connected sentences. Five-to-six sentence coherent speech is typical of this age, not a later one.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 4. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: As per Lev Vygotsky, as children grow, their language develops from _____.
think out loud to inner speech

explanation.en: Vygotsky held that speech begins as social (external) speech, then becomes private speech — children 'think out loud' to guide themselves — and finally turns into silent inner speech, which works as thought.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 5. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Piaget described cognitive development as occurring
as resolution of conflict at eight stages
in a continuous manner from birth through adulthood

explanation.en: Piaget described four qualitatively different stages: sensorimotor, pre-operational, concrete operational and formal operational. Option 3 describes Erikson's eight psychosocial stages, and option 4 describes a continuous (non-stage) view of development.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 6. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Rama was mean to her brother Tahir. Next day Tahir got sick. Rama concluded that she made her brother sick. According to Piaget, which stage of cognitive development is Rama in?

explanation.en: Linking two unrelated events — being mean to her brother and his falling sick — shows the faulty, magical cause-and-effect reasoning and egocentrism that Piaget described in the pre-operational stage (about 2 to 7 years).

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 7. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: _____ is the process by which children become aware of their gender roles.

explanation.en: Gender typing is the process through which children learn the roles, behaviours and attitudes their society considers appropriate for their gender. Equality, relatedness and homogeneity are not names of this process.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 8. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following scenarios is aptly describing the application of Lev Vygotsky's concept of ‘scaffolding’?
A teacher gave half-solved problems to her students who were finding it difficult to solve them otherwise.
A teacher has strictly prohibited students to have any kind of collaborations and communication with their peers.
A teacher has written answers on the blackboard and has asked the students to copy the answers passively in their notebooks.
A teacher has made it mandatory for her students to solve problems on their own in a set time period.

explanation.en: Scaffolding is temporary support matched to what a learner can do with help (the zone of proximal development), withdrawn as the learner gains skill. Giving half-solved problems to students who could not solve them alone is such support; banning collaboration, copying answers or forcing solo timed work is not.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 9. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Progressive education is an educational philosophy that emphasizes on _____.
standardized testing and strict curriculum guidelines

explanation.en: Progressive education, associated with John Dewey, puts the learner at the centre and emphasises learning through experience, activity and participation, rather than rote memorisation, testing or competition.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 10. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Read the following statements :
Assertion (A) : Children progress from understanding consequences of act to determine whether they are good/bad to understanding that rules and laws are flexible and can be changed.
Reason (R) : According to Kohlberg, children's moral development occurs in continuous manner and not a discontinuous one.
Choose the correct option.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are false.

explanation.en: A is true: in Kohlberg's theory children move from judging actions by their consequences to understanding that rules are social agreements that can change. R is false: Kohlberg described moral development as a sequence of distinct stages, which is a discontinuous view.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 11. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: According to Lev Vygotsky, cognitive development is guided by
language in the form of private speech
positive and negative reinforcement given by the environment

explanation.en: For Vygotsky, language is the main tool of thought. Private speech — children talking to themselves — guides and regulates their thinking. Assimilation and accommodation are Piaget's ideas, and reinforcement belongs to behaviourism.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 12. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following intelligence helps people to perceive, express, understand and regulate moods and feelings of others?

explanation.en: In Gardner's theory, interpersonal intelligence is the ability to understand other people's moods, feelings, intentions and motivations and to respond to them well. The other options are different intelligences.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 13. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: A child's first experience as well as expectations of what it means to be a ‘girl’ or a ‘boy’ comes from

explanation.en: The family is the first and most important agent of socialisation. Children's earliest ideas of what it means to be a 'girl' or a 'boy' come from how their family treats them and what it expects of them; media, relatives and neighbours influence them later.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 14. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: An essential characteristic of formative assessment is—
to assign relative ranks and positions to learners.
tests and exams at the end of the year.
clarification of assessment criteria to the learners.
to focus on quantitative means to achieve objectivity.

explanation.en: Formative assessment is assessment for learning: it is ongoing, gives feedback, and makes the criteria for good work clear to learners so they can improve. Ranking learners, year-end exams and a purely quantitative focus belong to summative assessment.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 15. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: A teacher should cater to _____ needs of gifted children in the classrooms.

explanation.en: Gifted children have cognitive needs (challenge and enrichment) but also social and emotional needs, such as finding peers they relate to and managing perfectionism or sensitivity. Teachers should cater to all three.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 17. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Which of the following are examples of pedagogical approaches to teach students with learning disabilities?
(i) Use of multisensory strategies
(ii) Standardized learning goals
(iii) Flexible and sequential instructions
(iv) Breaking down tasks into smaller parts
Choose the correct option.

explanation.en: Children with learning disabilities benefit from multisensory teaching, flexible and step-by-step instructions, and tasks broken into smaller parts. Standardised, identical learning goals for everyone do not meet their individual needs.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 18. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following statements about Autism Spectrum Disorder is correct?
Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder have excellent communication skills but very poor memory.
Sensory integration and regulation help children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
It is primarily the ability to hear that is affected in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder exhibit a preference for new stimuli every day.

explanation.en: Many children with Autism Spectrum Disorder process sensory input differently, so sensory integration and regulation strategies help them. ASD mainly affects social communication and interaction (not hearing), and children with ASD usually prefer routine and sameness rather than new stimuli.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 19. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: While teaching in inclusive setups, it is important that teachers—
see diversity as an obstacle to effective teaching.
continuously examine their own implicit and preconceived bias.
understand special children as needy and dependent on others.
follow same curriculum and uniform pedagogy of all learners.

explanation.en: Inclusive teaching asks teachers to keep examining their own hidden biases and assumptions about learners. Diversity should be seen as a resource, children with special needs should not be viewed as helpless, and teaching should be adapted to different learners rather than uniform.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 20. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Read the following statements :
Assertion (A) : Teachers should include a variety of children's literature to create print-rich environment in the classroom.
Reason (R) : Classrooms rich in literacy materials and literacy experiences are central to effective learning.
Choose the correct option.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are false.

explanation.en: A print-rich classroom with varied children's literature gives children constant, meaningful contact with reading and writing. Because classrooms rich in literacy materials and experiences are central to effective learning, R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 21. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: In order to facilitate students' learning in a progressive classroom, a teacher should emphasize on the practice of

explanation.en: A progressive classroom values inquiry, discussion and reflection. Encouraging reflective thinking helps students examine their own ideas and learn from experience; conditioning, passive copying and obedient listening do not.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 22. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Seeing Raman, a 4th grade student stuck on a question, his teacher asked him to try the solution while speaking what is going on in his mind. Such verbalization is likely to be—
futile because language hinders thought process.
helpful because language facilitates thought process.
supportive only for students with learning disabilities because they have difficulty in auditory processing.
unproductive because language and thought are not related.

explanation.en: Speaking one's thoughts aloud is private speech, which Vygotsky saw as a tool that organises and guides thinking. So verbalising his steps is likely to help Raman solve the problem.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 23. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: A teacher who believes in constructivist pedagogy would—
avoid connecting content to real world.
avoid judgements of students solely on the basis of socio-cultural backgrounds.
promote high levels of verbal instructions as primary pedagogy.

explanation.en: A constructivist teacher respects how each child builds knowledge and does not judge students on the basis of their socio-cultural background. Such a teacher connects content to the real world, limits lecturing and avoids rigid ability grouping.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 24. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Active engagement of learners implies that the students—
consider textbook as the sole source of knowledge.

explanation.en: Active engagement means learners take part in building their own knowledge — they inquire, explore and ask questions — rather than memorising facts, chasing marks or relying only on the textbook.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 25. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Radha reasons, "Clothes dry faster in the sun than in the shade, so the sun is helping them to dry". She is showing an understanding of—

explanation.en: Radha compares the sun and the shade and links a cause (the sun's heat) to an effect (clothes drying faster). This is an understanding of cause and effect.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 26. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following is an example of intrinsic motivation?
Studying for a test to get good grade
Playing a game for the prize money
Playing a sport for personal enjoyment
Completing the homework to avoid being scolded by parents

explanation.en: Intrinsic motivation comes from within — doing something because it is enjoyable or satisfying in itself. Studying for grades, playing for prize money and avoiding scolding are driven by external rewards or punishments (extrinsic motivation).

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 27. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Read the following statements :
Assertion (A) : Teachers who believe in constructivist pedagogy should provide a lot of materials to the children.
Reason (R) : Young children depend solely on verbal instructions and lectures for meaningful learning.
Choose the correct option.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are false.

explanation.en: A is true: constructivist teachers give children many materials to explore and build understanding. R is false: young children learn meaningfully through concrete, hands-on experience, not only through verbal instructions and lectures.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 28. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Avoiding the appearance of low ability in front of peers and teachers is an example of

explanation.en: Performance-avoidance goals are about avoiding looking incompetent in front of others. Mastery and task-involved goals focus on learning itself, and performance-approach goals focus on appearing more able than others.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 29. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following is an effective way to promote critical thinking in the classroom?
Encouraging students to think independently and questioning assumptions.
Providing students with a set of predetermined answers to choose from.

explanation.en: Critical thinking grows when students think independently, ask questions and examine assumptions. Rote memorisation, discouraging questions and fixed answers work against it.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 30. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: What is the sum of all the prime numbers between 12 and 49?

explanation.en: The primes between 12 and 49 are 13, 17, 19, 23, 29, 31, 37, 41, 43 and 47. Their sum is 300.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 31. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: If 101 × 210 − 120 × 102 = 99 × 104 − □, then what is the number at □?

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 32. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: The sum of all the common factors of 36 and 48 (excluding 1) is

explanation.en: The common factors of 36 and 48 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. Leaving out 1: 2 + 3 + 4 + 6 + 12 = 27.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 33. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: What is the difference between the greatest 4-digit number and the least 4-digit number formed by using the digits 1, 5, 0 and 7 once?

explanation.en: The greatest number using 1, 5, 0 and 7 once is 7510. The least 4-digit number cannot start with 0, so it is 1057. Difference: 7510 − 1057 = 6453.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 34. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Kanta has five dozen chocolates. She gives 1/6 of these to Aruna and 1/5 of the remaining chocolates to Radha. She then gives 1/8 of the remaining chocolates to each of her other three friends. How many chocolates does Kanta have now?

explanation.en: Five dozen = 60. Aruna gets 1/6 of 60 = 10, leaving 50. Radha gets 1/5 of 50 = 10, leaving 40. Each of three friends gets 1/8 of 40 = 5, so 15 more are given away. Kanta has 40 − 15 = 25.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 35. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: (LCM of 96, 120 and 160) ÷ (HCF of 72 and 168) is equal to

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 36. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: The cost of 8 Samosas is ₹ 156 and that of 4 Idlis is ₹ 98. Sunita has a ₹ 200 note only and buys 3 Samosas and 3 Idlis. How much money is left with her now?

explanation.en: One samosa costs 156 ÷ 8 = ₹ 19.50 and one idli costs 98 ÷ 4 = ₹ 24.50. Three of each cost 3 × (19.50 + 24.50) = ₹ 132. Money left = 200 − 132 = ₹ 68.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 37. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: 24 L 650 mL of milk is filled in 29 bottles each of same size. The quantity of milk in 15 such bottles is

explanation.en: 24 L 650 mL = 24650 mL, so each bottle holds 24650 ÷ 29 = 850 mL. Fifteen bottles hold 15 × 850 = 12750 mL = 12 L 750 mL.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 38. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: The internal length, breadth and height of a cuboidal box are 12 cm, 10 cm and 8 cm, respectively. A cubical box has side (internal) 9 cm. Avin tries to pack 1800 cubical dice of side 1 cm each in these two boxes. The number of dice which are left unpacked is :

explanation.en: The cuboidal box holds 12 × 10 × 8 = 960 dice and the cubical box holds 9 × 9 × 9 = 729 dice, 1689 in all. Dice left unpacked = 1800 − 1689 = 111.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 39. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: A bag containing potatoes, onions and lemons weighs 46 kg 160 g. The weight of potatoes is 17 kg 115 g and that of onions is 15 kg 325 g. The weight of empty bag is 120 g. If 30 lemons weigh 1 kg, then what is the number of lemons in the bag?

explanation.en: Weight of lemons = 46160 g − 17115 g − 15325 g − 120 g = 13600 g = 13.6 kg. Since 30 lemons weigh 1 kg, there are 13.6 × 30 = 408 lemons.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 40. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Which of the following has/have only two lines of symmetry?
A. Equilateral triangle
B. Rectangle
C. Rhombus
D. Isosceles triangle
Choose the correct option.

explanation.en: A rectangle (not a square) and a rhombus (not a square) each have exactly two lines of symmetry. An equilateral triangle has three and an isosceles triangle has one, so the answer is B and C.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 41. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following letters has a rotational symmetry but no line symmetry?

explanation.en: The letter Z looks the same after a half turn (rotational symmetry of order 2), but no line divides it into mirror halves. X and O have both kinds of symmetry, and M has a vertical line of symmetry but no rotational symmetry.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 42. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: A pentagonal pyramid has (2) six faces and six edges

explanation.en: A pentagonal pyramid has a pentagonal base and five triangular faces (6 faces), five base corners plus the apex (6 vertices), and 10 edges. So it has six vertices and six faces.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 43. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
The following table shows the number of visitors to a library in the first six days of a week:
Days — Number of visitors
Monday — 86
Tuesday — 114
Wednesday — 141
Thursday — 95
Friday — 124
Saturday — 151
On which day, the number of visitors to the library was 29 more than its previous day?

explanation.en: Day-to-day increases: Tuesday +28, Wednesday +27, Thursday −46, Friday +29 (124 − 95), Saturday +27. Friday had 29 more visitors than the previous day.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 44. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: The sum of next two numbers in the pattern 3, 10, 32, 99, _____, _____ is

explanation.en: Each term is 3 times the previous term plus 1, 2, 3, … in turn: 3 × 3 + 1 = 10, 10 × 3 + 2 = 32, 32 × 3 + 3 = 99. Next: 99 × 3 + 4 = 301 and 301 × 3 + 5 = 908. Their sum is 1209.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 45. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: A teacher writes the number 308 on the blackboard and asks the children to read the number loudly. A child says, “It is thirty-eight.” Which among the following is the most appropriate strategy to rectify the error committed by the child?
Ask another child to read the number loudly.
Provide few practical examples to the child to understand the position of digits in a number.
Teacher can read the number once and ask the child to repeat.
Ask the child to start counting from 99 up to 308 in continuity.

explanation.en: Reading 308 as 'thirty-eight' shows the child has not understood place value — that the 3 stands for 3 hundreds and the 0 holds the tens place. Concrete examples (such as bundles of sticks or place-value cards) build this understanding; repeating after the teacher or counting does not address the gap.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 46. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
A class II mathematics teacher gives the following word problem on addition to the students to solve : “A bag contains 4 mangoes and 6 more mangoes are added to it. How many total mangoes are there in the bag?”
This type of word problem belongs to which of the following structures of addition?

explanation.en: The problem starts with a quantity (4 mangoes) and increases it by adding more (6 mangoes). This 'change-increase' structure is called augmentation. Aggregation would combine two separate groups into one.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 47. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following pre-number concepts are relevant for building the understanding of mathematical concepts at foundational stage?

explanation.en: Pre-number concepts such as classification (sorting by attributes), ordering or seriation, matching and one-to-one correspondence lay the foundation for number sense at the foundational stage. Operations and place value come after these.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 48. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following is least desirable in a primary school mathematics classroom?
Encouragement of intuitive concepts in the classroom
Building linkages with real-life situations involving mathematical ideas
Including open discussions on problem solving in the classroom

explanation.en: Mechanically solving algorithm-based workbook questions does little to build understanding. Intuitive ideas, links to real life and open discussion on problem solving are all desirable in a primary mathematics classroom.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 49. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Which of the following is/are appropriate in the context of social perspectives on assessment in mathematics?
A. Bringing the experiences of children outside the school in assessment
B. Making standardized tests
C. Using folk algorithms from different cultures
Choose the correct option.

explanation.en: A social perspective on assessment values the mathematics children meet outside school, including folk algorithms from different cultures. Standardised tests do not take this perspective, so the answer is A and C.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 50. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following is least appropriate about contextual problems in mathematics?
They are connected closely to children's lives.
They can help in developing the children's ability of mathematical modelling.
Children tend to focus on getting a correct answer while solving them.
They might be derived from recent experiences in the classroom like a field trip, a discussion in art, science, or social studies classrooms.

explanation.en: Contextual problems are linked to children's lives, help develop mathematical modelling and can come from classroom experiences. Their purpose is to shift attention to understanding the situation, not just getting a correct answer — so statement 3 is the least appropriate.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 51. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
The statements given below are marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (B) :
A : It is important to introduce data representation and analysis in the primary stage and to strengthen it in the upper primary stage.
B : Data analysis exposes children at primary level to uncertainty and changeability in information as opposed to the fixed nature of mathematical facts they mostly study.
Choose the correct option.
A is true and B is false.
A is false and B is true.
A is true but B is not the correct reason of A.
A is true and B is the correct reason of A.

explanation.en: Data representation and analysis should begin at the primary stage and be strengthened at the upper primary stage. The reason given is the correct one: working with data shows children that information can be uncertain and variable, unlike the fixed facts they mostly study.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 52. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following is not an expected learning outcome for class III as per NCERT recommendations?
Extend the sequence A, DE, HIJ, _____ .
There are 12 balls in a box. How many balls will be there in 5 such boxes?

explanation.en: Commutativity of multiplication, extending letter patterns and simple multiplication word problems are expected at class III. Dividing fractions, such as 1/2 ÷ 1/3, belongs to much later classes, so it is not a class III learning outcome.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 53. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following mathematical statements is true?
Zero is called an additive identity for whole numbers.
Mathematics is based only on observations and experiments.
Zero is called the multiplicative identity for whole numbers.
Commutative law holds true for the operation of ‘division’.

explanation.en: Zero is the additive identity for whole numbers because a + 0 = a. One (not zero) is the multiplicative identity, division is not commutative, and mathematics rests on logical reasoning, not only on observation and experiment.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 54. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: In mathematics, the primary stage curriculum is focussed on _____.

explanation.en: Primary mathematics should nurture children's curiosity and enjoyment of mathematics, building understanding through exploration rather than rote learning, written algorithms or textbook drill.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 55. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: A child writes five hundred three as 5003. It shows that
the child needs to learn counting
the child does not know how to write numbers in words
the child does not know the concept of place value
the child needs to learn recognition of digits

explanation.en: Writing 'five hundred three' as 5003 shows the child writes 500 and then 3 instead of using place value to show 5 hundreds, 0 tens and 3 ones. The difficulty is with the concept of place value.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 56. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: According to Van Hiele's levels of development of geometrical thinking, which of the following represents level–2 (relationships)?
A child cannot classify various shapes that look similar.
A child identifies and classifies shapes based only on their size or orientation.
A child can informally deduce general properties of a given geometrical shape and is able to see the linkages among these properties.
A student can follow the deductive axiomatic systems of geometry.

explanation.en: Van Hiele's levels are visualisation, analysis, informal deduction (relationships), formal deduction and rigour. At the relationships level, a child can informally deduce properties of shapes and see the links between them. Option 4 describes a later level and options 1 and 2 earlier ones.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 57. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following is the most appropriate example of incorporation of local/cultural knowledge in mathematics teaching-learning?
Colourful mathematics textbooks with pictures from various cultures
Including only traditional methods of calculations in textbooks
Remedial teaching for learners from different cultures
Including examples of different methods of calculation used by the people from various occupations and communities

explanation.en: Bringing in the calculation methods used by people of different occupations and communities connects mathematics to children's own cultures and lives. Pictures alone, only traditional methods or remedial teaching do not draw on local knowledge in this way.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 58. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: One of the main guiding principles of the National Education Policy, 2020 is “The highest priority is to achieve foundational literacy and numeracy at _____ by all the students”.

explanation.en: NEP 2020 makes foundational literacy and numeracy the highest priority, to be achieved by all students by grade 3.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 59. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: A primary class mathematics teacher brings in two jars of different shapes, with water in one of them, to her classroom. She pours water completely from the taller, thin jar to the shorter, broad jar. She then asks the question, “Which jar can hold more water?” This activity is most appropriate to teach
how to calculate the area of two jars with different shapes
the concept of standard units of measurement of liquids

explanation.en: Pouring the same water from a tall, thin jar into a short, broad jar shows that the amount stays the same even though it looks different. This activity teaches volume and its conservation.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 60. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: The approximate distance between the capital of Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal) and the capital of Maharashtra (Mumbai) is 756 km. If a train covers this distance in nearly 14 hours, the average speed of the train in metre per second is

explanation.en: Average speed = 756 km ÷ 14 h = 54 km/h. Converting: 54 × 1000 m ÷ 3600 s = 15 m/s.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 61. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Consider the following characteristics of houses :
A. Wooden floor and wooden flat ceilings
B. Ground floor without window for animals and storing necessary materials
C. Elevated houses made with slanting roofs and the stone pillars
D. Thick walls made of stones, mud and lime
The characteristics found in the houses of Leh and Ladakh are

explanation.en: Ladakh is a cold desert, so houses have thick walls of stone, mud and lime to keep warm, wooden floors and flat wooden ceilings (flat roofs suit the little rain there), and a ground floor without windows for animals and storage. Raised houses with slanting roofs suit places with heavy rain, not Ladakh.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 62. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Select from the following a state where the meaning of ‘Torang’ is jungle

explanation.en: This question is based on the NCERT Class V EVS textbook chapter 'Whose Forests?'. Suryamani, from Jharkhand, explains that her organisation is named 'Torang', which means jungle.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 63. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Consider the following statements about Nepenthes/Pitcher plant :
A. This plant has leaves which are pitcher-shaped and the mouth is covered with a leaf.
B. This plant has a special smell that attracts insects to it.
C. This plant is very common in the cold deserts of Ladakh and Russia.
D. This plant can trap and eat small insects, frogs and even mice. These animals when land on the mouth of the plant, they get trapped and cannot get out of it.
The correct statements are

explanation.en: The pitcher plant has pitcher-shaped leaves with a lid-like cover, attracts insects with its smell, and traps and digests small animals such as insects and even frogs. It grows in warm, humid places, not in cold deserts, so statement C is wrong.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 64. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which one of the following statements is not true about the houses of Srinagar in Kashmir?
The old houses here are made of stone, bricks and wood.
Some old houses have special type of windows which come out of the wall. These are called ‘dab’.
Houseboats on Dal Lake are one of the attractions of Srinagar.
Many families in Srinagar live in ‘Dongas’ which are built in hilly areas.

explanation.en: In Srinagar, 'Dongas' are boats on which many families live on the lake, not houses built in hilly areas. The other statements — stone, brick and wood houses, 'dab' windows and the Dal Lake houseboats — are true.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 65. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Consider the following statements about beehives :
A. Every beehive has only one queen bee that lays eggs.
B. There are a few males in the hive who make the hive.
C. The number of females is much more than the males in the hive. These female bees are the worker bees who work all day. They also look after the baby bees.
D. The worker bees fly around flowers in search of nectar for honey. On finding flowers with nectar, they do a special kind of dance by which other bees also join them to collect the nectar.
The correct statements are

explanation.en: The CBSE final answer key gives option 4 (A and D). A is correct: a hive has one queen who lays eggs. D is correct: worker bees search for nectar and dance to show other bees where the flowers are. B is wrong, because the hive is built by the worker bees, not by the males. Note: statement C (worker bees are females, far outnumber the males and look after the young) is also generally true of honeybees, so this answer may be disputed; it is shown here exactly as CBSE published it.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 66. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Consider the following statements about elephants :
A. Elephants live in herds.
B. A herd may have 20 to 25 female elephants and their young ones.
C. Male elephants live in the herd till they are 9–10 years.
D. The oldest female takes all the decisions of the herd.
The correct statements are

explanation.en: Elephants live in herds, and the oldest female leads the herd and takes its decisions. Statements B and C give the herd size and the age at which males leave the herd incorrectly, so the answer is A and D.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 67. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
More than a thousand years ago, Al-Biruni, a traveller from Uzbekistan, had described his observations about India. Which of the following observations were recorded in Al-Biruni's book?
A. People of India are very skilled at making ponds.
B. Horses are used to draw carts in India.
C. Step-wells have separate steps for going up and coming down.
D. Lakes and Johads are built to collect water.
Choose the correct option.

explanation.en: Al-Biruni, who visited India about a thousand years ago, wrote that its people were very skilled at building ponds and tanks, and described tanks with separate steps for going up and coming down. This appears in the NCERT Class V EVS chapter 'Every Drop Counts'.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 68. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: People who have been living in the forests for at least _____ have a right over the forest land and what is grown on it, according to the Right to Forest Act, 2007.

explanation.en: This question follows the NCERT Class V EVS chapter 'Whose Forests?', which states that under the Right to Forest Act passed in 2007, people who have lived in a forest for at least 25 years have a right over the forest land and what grows on it.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 69. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Read Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully :
Assertion (A) : Domestication of animals was a gradual process that took place in many parts of the world.
Reason (R) : The earliest domesticated animals include sheep and goat.
Choose the correct option.
Both A and R are true and R explains A.
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

explanation.en: Both statements are true: domestication happened slowly in many parts of the world, and sheep and goats were among the earliest domesticated animals. But R only names early domesticated animals; it does not explain why domestication was gradual.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 70. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which one of the following animals was not reared by the Harappans?

explanation.en: Harappans reared sheep, goats, cattle and buffalo. There is no clear evidence that they reared horses.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 71. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following States/Union Territories were carved out in the Indian Union in the last 25 years?
Jammu and Kashmir, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh

explanation.en: Chhattisgarh became a state in 2000, Telangana in 2014 and Ladakh a Union Territory in 2019. Puducherry, Goa, Sikkim, Madhya Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Arunachal Pradesh were formed earlier.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 72. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: You must have heard about the famous Olympian Karnam Malleswari. What game did she play in international events?

explanation.en: Karnam Malleswari is a weightlifter. She won a bronze medal at the 2000 Sydney Olympics, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 73. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which one of the following statements is true about Madhubani paintings and the area in which they originated?
It is an old form of folk art that originated in the State of Rajasthan.
These paintings are done on the floor using brush and indigo in the Mithila region of Bihar.
These paintings are mainly influenced by the Mughal art and culture.
It has its roots in the Mithila region of Bihar and these are made out of paste of powdered rice in which colours are mixed.

explanation.en: Madhubani (Mithila) painting comes from the Mithila region of Bihar. It was traditionally made with a paste of powdered rice mixed with colours. It is not from Rajasthan, not based on Mughal art, and not floor painting with brush and indigo.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 74. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Read Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully :
Assertion (A) : Mixture of cow dung and mud is used to coat the floor of houses.
Reason (R) : Cow dung helps to regulate the temperature inside the house and keeps the insects away.
Choose the correct option.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

explanation.en: Floors are coated with a mixture of cow dung and mud because cow dung helps keep the inside of the house cool and keeps insects away. So R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 75. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Match Column–A with Column–B:
Column–A: (a) Peer assessment  (b) Rubric-based rating scale  (c) Assessment as learning  (d) Paper-pencil test
Column–B: (i) Tool of assessment  (ii) Self-learning  (iii) Summative assessment  (iv) Technique of assessment
Choose the correct option.

explanation.en: Peer assessment is a technique of assessment; a rubric-based rating scale is a tool of assessment; assessment as learning means learners reflect on and direct their own learning (self-learning); and a paper-pencil test is typically used for summative assessment. This matches option 3.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 76. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Which of the following statements are correct about learning of EVS?
A. Children are naturally curious to learn.
B. Children are passive recipients in learning.
C. Children need teacher for learning.
D. Children learn better in collaborative groups.
Choose the correct option.

explanation.en: Children are naturally curious and learn well in collaborative groups. They are active learners rather than passive recipients, and they also learn outside the teacher's presence, so A and D are correct.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 77. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Which of the following components best describe the meaning of EVS?
A. Accumulation of facts
B. Observation
C. Asking questions
D. Experimentation
Choose the correct option.

explanation.en: EVS is about observing, asking questions and experimenting to understand one's surroundings. Merely accumulating facts is not its purpose, so B, C and D best describe it.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 78. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: The knowledge of which of the following is the most important for an EVS teacher?
Facts, principles and laws of EVS

explanation.en: Knowing how children learn EVS — their ideas, experiences and ways of making sense of the world — is the most important knowledge for an EVS teacher, because it shapes how content and teaching methods are chosen.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 79. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Harleen asked her teacher, "Why do roses have thorns?" What must be the pedagogy of an EVS teacher towards this curiosity?
Tell that roses have thorns to protect itself from animals.
Tell that all roses do not have thorns.
Tell her to find out which other plants have thorns.
Ask her to observe animals eating plants with and without thorns.

explanation.en: Letting Harleen observe animals eating plants with and without thorns allows her to find the answer through her own observation and inquiry, which is the aim of EVS pedagogy. Simply telling her the answer ends her curiosity.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 80. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Isha of class IV asked her teacher, "Why cow does not lay eggs?" What is your most appropriate response if you are Isha's teacher?
Reply that cows are mammals which give birth to young ones.
Ask her to relate laying of eggs/giving birth to their visible ears and whose ears cannot be seen.
Ask her to find out herself the reason for this.
Ask other students of the class to answer Isha's question.

explanation.en: Guiding Isha to notice a pattern herself — animals with visible ears, like cows, usually give birth, while animals whose ears cannot be seen, like birds, usually lay eggs — builds observation and reasoning instead of just handing her an answer.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 81. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
An EVS teacher wants to use storytelling as a strategy for teaching and learning. Which of the following are the most suitable for this?
A. Contextual stories
B. Folk stories
C. Student-written stories
D. Stories focussing on morals
Choose the correct option.

explanation.en: Contextual stories, folk stories and stories written by students connect EVS to children's lives and cultures. Stories mainly meant to teach morals are less suited to building EVS concepts, so the answer is A, B and C.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 82. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Teacher asked students to draw an animal. Poonam draws an animal, having body parts of different animals. What should the teacher do?
A. Scold Poonam for drawing an absurd animal.
B. Ask Poonam why she has drawn parts of different animals.
C. Tell Poonam that no such animal exists.
D. Ask Poonam the name of the animal she has drawn.
Choose the correct option.

explanation.en: The teacher should respect Poonam's imagination and understand her thinking by asking why she combined parts of different animals and what she calls it. Scolding her or saying such an animal doesn't exist would discourage her creativity.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 83. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
If a teacher wants that students learn about the plant diversity, which of the following are the most suitable activities for this?
A. Ask students to look for objects which have patterns of leaves on them in their house.
B. Recite a poem to students written on different types of plants and their characteristics.
C. Blindfold students and ask the students to identify plants by smelling crushed leaves.
D. Ask students to collect the leaves of plants and make pictures of different animals using the leaves.
Choose the correct option.

explanation.en: Identifying plants by the smell of crushed leaves and making pictures from collected leaves are hands-on activities that let children experience the variety of plants directly. So C and D are the most suitable.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 84. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Which of the following elements best describe the nature of EVS?
A. Established facts
B. Logical information
C. Observation
D. Scientific terminology
E. Experimentation
Choose the correct option.

explanation.en: EVS is learnt by observing and experimenting with one's surroundings. Established facts, mere information and scientific terminology are not its essence, so the answer is C and E.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 85. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Read the following statements A and B carefully :
A. Recommendation of NCF (2005) is to discourage rote learning of information.
B. Recommendation of NCF (2005) is to discourage maintenance of sharp boundaries between different subject areas.
Choose the correct option. (2) Both A and B are false.
Both A and B are true.
Both A and B are false.
A is true but B is false.
A is false but B is true.

explanation.en: NCF 2005 recommends moving away from rote learning and softening the sharp boundaries between subjects so that knowledge is connected. Both statements are true.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 86. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Chinu wants to know how day and night occur. Which of the following methods will be the best to explain this to Chinu?

explanation.en: A working model, such as a globe turned in front of a lamp, lets Chinu see how the Earth's rotation causes day and night. It makes the idea concrete in a way diagrams or stories cannot.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 87. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Read the following statements A and B carefully :
A. In EVS learning, the challenge is to respect the multicultural dimensions of diverse classrooms.
B. In EVS learning, every student should feel important—community, culture and his way of life.
Choose the correct option. (2) Both A and B are false.
Both A and B are true.
Both A and B are false.
A is true but B is false.
A is false but B is true.

explanation.en: EVS classrooms bring together children of many cultures, and respecting this diversity is a challenge teachers must meet. Every child should feel that their community, culture and way of life matter. Both statements are true.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 88. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en:
Discussion is used by the EVS teachers in their classes because
A. discussion develops social interaction among children
B. discussion supports authentic and meaningful learning
C. meaningful construction of knowledge occurs when ideas are shared
D. discussion is suitable for the emotionally balanced children
Choose the correct option.

explanation.en: Discussion builds social interaction, supports authentic and meaningful learning, and helps children construct knowledge by sharing ideas. It suits all children, not only emotionally balanced ones, so the answer is A, B and C.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 89. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: An environmental studies teacher asked his class III children to visit the school garden and collect different types of leaves. Which of the following process skills does the teacher want to develop among children?
Creative expression and experimentation with leaves

explanation.en: Collecting different types of leaves requires children to observe their features and sort them into groups, so the activity develops observation and classification.

questions.source: CBSE, CTET February 2026, Paper I, Set S (7 Feb 2026), question 90. Answer from the CBSE final answer key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Who gave the concept of multiple intelligence?
text.hi: किसने बहुविमात्मक प्रज्ञा का प्रत्यय दिया?

explanation.en: Howard Gardner proposed the theory of multiple intelligences in "Frames of Mind" (1983). He described linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, bodily-kinaesthetic, musical, interpersonal, intrapersonal and naturalist intelligences. Spearman is known for the two-factor theory and Goleman for emotional intelligence.
explanation.hi: बहुबुद्धि (बहुविमात्मक प्रज्ञा) का सिद्धांत हॉवर्ड गार्डनर ने 1983 में "फ्रेम्स ऑफ माइंड" में दिया। उन्होंने भाषायी, तार्किक-गणितीय, स्थानिक, शारीरिक-गतिक, संगीतात्मक, अंतर्वैयक्तिक, अंतःवैयक्तिक और प्रकृतिवादी बुद्धि बताई। स्पीयरमैन द्वि-कारक सिद्धांत और गोलमैन संवेगात्मक बुद्धि के लिए जाने जाते हैं।

questions.source: UPTET 2019 (Uttar Pradesh Teacher Eligibility Test), held on 8 January 2020 by the Pariksha Niyamak Pradhikari (Examination Regulatory Authority), Uttar Pradesh, Prayagraj. Primary level paper, question 1. Answer as given in the solved paper's key, still to be checked against the official final key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.hi: डिस्लेक्सिया में यह करने में कठिनाई होती है–

explanation.en: Dyslexia is a learning disability that mainly affects reading and spelling: the child finds it hard to link letters with their sounds, confuses or reverses letters, and reads slowly.
explanation.hi: डिस्लेक्सिया एक अधिगम अक्षमता है जिसमें मुख्य रूप से पढ़ने और वर्तनी में कठिनाई होती है। बच्चा अक्षरों को उनकी ध्वनियों से जोड़ने में कठिनाई महसूस करता है, अक्षरों को उलट-पलट देता है और धीरे पढ़ता है।

questions.source: UPTET 2019 (Uttar Pradesh Teacher Eligibility Test), held on 8 January 2020 by the Pariksha Niyamak Pradhikari (Examination Regulatory Authority), Uttar Pradesh, Prayagraj. Primary level paper, question 2. Answer as given in the solved paper's key, still to be checked against the official final key. Explanation written by UPTET Saathi.

text.en: Which of the following is not the role of teacher in inclusive classroom?
text.hi: निम्न में से क्या समावेशी कक्षा में शिक्षक की भूमिका नहीं है?

text.en: Make adequate seating arrangements according to the requirement of the child
text.hi: बच्चे की आवश्यकता के अनुरूप बैठने की पर्याप्त व्यवस्था करनी चाहिए

text.en: Teacher should not pay attention to differently abled child
text.hi: शिक्षक को निःशक्त बच्चों पर ध्यान नहीं देना चाहिए
शिक्षक को बच्चों को प्रोत्साहित करना चाहिए
